name: Citizenship by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: Anyone whose father is Iranian is Iranian, regardless of the child's country of birth (Civil Code Article 976(2)). This is the automatic, default rule -- descent through the father alone.

requirement_groups.name: Maternal descent (2006 amendment, opt-in at age 18)

requirements.blocker_text: A person born to an Iranian mother and a non-Iranian father is not automatically Iranian at birth under the base Article 976 rule. A 2006 amendment allows such a person to apply for Iranian nationality upon reaching age 18, subject to conditions including having no criminal record and, in practice, completing renunciation or other administrative formalities; this is a discretionary, application-based opt-in, not an automatic acquisition, and does not retroactively apply to those already adult before the amendment without going through this same application process.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for Iranian nationality after turning 18, if born to an Iranian mother and non-Iranian father.

evidence_required.document: Parent's proof of Iranian nationality (Shenasnameh/national ID)

sources.title: Iran Data Portal (Syracuse University academic archive) -- English translation of Iran's Civil Code, Article 976: nationality provisions including Article 976(2)'s paternal-descent rule ('anyone whose father is Iranian'), plus the 2006 amendment permitting persons born to an Iranian mother and foreign father to apply for Iranian nationality at age 18

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Iran). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to an academic archive (tier 3) hosting an English translation of the Civil Code rather than a fetched government original (an Iranian Parliament/Ministry of Justice source for the Civil Code was not successfully retrieved in this build). MARQUEE GENDERED FINDING: Iran's default descent rule is paternal-only -- a child of an Iranian father is automatically a citizen regardless of birth country, while a child of an Iranian mother and foreign father is NOT automatically a citizen at all under the base rule. The 2006 amendment is a narrow, application-based, age-18 opt-in exception for the maternal-line case, not a repeal of the underlying paternal rule or a route to automatic acquisition at birth -- this is a materially weaker fix than the gender-neutral descent reforms seen elsewhere in this dataset (Kenya, Pakistan post-2000, India post-1992, Tunisia post-2010). dual_citizenship_allowed deliberately left null at the route level rather than asserted either way: Iran's Civil Code Article 976(6)/Article 989 framework treats unauthorized acquisition of a second nationality by an Iranian citizen as generally invalid and subject to serious consequences (see ir_citizenship_naturalisation.json's notes on the renunciation regime), so whether a person acquiring Iranian nationality through this descent route may ALSO hold another nationality is genuinely conditional/restricted rather than a simple yes or no -- modeling it as a flat boolean here would overstate certainty either way.
